title: Work Experience
description: My professional journey in reverse chronological order.

experienceGroups.subtitle: The "People Leadership" Era 🏕️
description: I'd been leading engineers informally for years, so I stepped into my first official engineering manager role, with engineers reporting to me. I coached a distributed team across Australia, New Zealand, and the UK, and set the direction and cadence they delivered against.

Together we took Canva's ADA goal from at risk to met, with WCAG 2.1 AA certification and a published VPAT in April 2026. We built the A11y Platform, which cut triage from hours to minutes across 63 teams, and I set the roadmap for what came next.

experienceGroups.subtitle: The "Design Systems" Era 🌲
description: I found my passion here. Design Systems is where I belong. It perfectly blends my Full Stack distributed systems thinking with scaling visual designs 🙌. There's a lot to grow into within the space. Design Tokens are where I went deepest. I founded Jarden's Frontend Guild, mentored four engineers at Xero (two were promoted), and directed 12+ contract engineers on a product-wide brand uplift.

experienceGroups.subtitle: The "Full Stack" Era 🪴
description: I learned I wanted to be closer to the end user and create the products they interact with. This narrowed my scope to product facing Full Stack roles. I played a key role in Starbucks' move from a monolith to a service-oriented architecture.
As I spent time in the Full Stack space, I gravitated towards the visual elements and building UIs that scale. This is what led me down the path of Design Systems.

experienceGroups.subtitle: Prologue: Finding My Path 🌱
description: As a fresh grad out of University, I had no idea of the software development landscape ahead of me. Getting into contracting and consulting in this early stage allowed me to attain a wide array of project experience.
